items.headline: Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat
items.summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, the closest Senate race in the country, according to an AP race call. He becomes the state's first Democratic senator in more than 40 years.

items.headline: White House warns Democrats on probes
items.summary: The White House counsel sent a letter warning Rep. Robert Garcia, the incoming House Oversight chair, about Democrats' planned investigations of the administration. Democrats take control of the House in January.

items.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to POW swap
items.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large prisoner-of-war exchange after U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, officials said. It was described as the largest humanitarian release since 2022.

items.headline: Bessent moves to military base
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved to a military base over safety concerns, according to an AP report. U.S. intelligence indicates Iran has stepped up efforts to target American officials.

items.headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza hospital
items.summary: An Israeli strike on a Gaza hospital killed six people, including a surgeon, and injured dozens, health authorities said. Israel said it was targeting a Hamas commander.

items.headline: Key races still uncalled a week on
items.summary: More than a dozen key races remained too early to call a week after Election Day, leaving the size of Democrats' majorities unsettled. In Alaska, a judge is weighing Mary Peltola's request for a list of voters whose absentee ballots were rejected.

items.headline: Education Dept. finalizes accreditation rule
items.summary: The Education Department has finalized a rule changing how colleges are accredited. President Trump had described accreditation as a way to reshape higher education.

items.headline: Biden says he would have stepped aside
items.summary: Former President Joe Biden said he would have stepped down had he known he had cancer. His prostate cancer diagnosis was disclosed in 2025, after he left office.

items.headline: Rare Death Valley pupfish rebounds
items.summary: The Devils Hole pupfish, which lives only in an underground cavern in Death Valley, is increasing in number. The species is among the rarest fish in the world.

items.headline: SS United States sunk to form reef
items.summary: The SS United States, once the world's fastest ocean liner, was sunk off Florida's Panhandle on Wednesday. It becomes the world's largest artificial reef.

digest.overview:
Democrat Scott Colom unseated Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, the nation's closest Senate race, becoming the state's first Democratic senator in more than four decades. More than a dozen House and Senate contests remain uncalled a week after Election Day, and a judge in Alaska is weighing Mary Peltola's bid to obtain a list of rejected absentee ballots. The White House counsel warned incoming House Oversight chair Robert Garcia over Democrats' plans to investigate the administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved to a military base after U.S. intelligence pointed to stepped-up Iranian efforts to target American officials. The Education Department finalized a rule overhauling college accreditation. Former President Joe Biden said he would have stepped down had he known he had cancer. President Trump laid a wreath at Arlington National Cemetery on Veterans Day. The SS United States, once the fastest ocean liner, was sunk off Florida to become an artificial reef.

Abroad, Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large prisoner-of-war exchange after U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, described as the biggest humanitarian release since 2022. An Israeli strike on a Gaza hospital killed six people, including a surgeon, health officials said; Israel said it targeted a Hamas commander. Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner is running for president of France. ExxonMobil signed a preliminary agreement to explore a return to Venezuela. A new estimate projects global fossil fuel emissions will fall in 2026.

home.overview:
The Lakers kept rolling with a 123–112 win in Milwaukee to reach 11-2, Boston edged Toronto 98–93 to move to 10-2, and Portland beat Oklahoma City for the second straight game, 118–108. Golden State fell 115–108 at Houston after Stephen Curry left early with an abdominal injury that has the Warriors worried, and Brooklyn hammered New Orleans 145–111. Four NBA games are on tonight before NBA Cup group play tips off Friday with nine games. Week 10 of the NFL opens tonight with Commanders at Giants; Arizona hands rookie Carson Beck his first start, Cleveland goes back to Deshaun Watson, and the Rams will be without Puka Nacua for several weeks. In baseball, Will Venable and Pat Murphy won Manager of the Year as the GM meetings roll on.

Club soccer is still on break, and the Nations League returns tonight: Harry Kane is set to break England's appearance record against Croatia at Wembley, Spain visit Czechia and Italy host France. Germany play Serbia on Friday, South Korea face Saudi Arabia in Doha, and the USMNT meet Haiti on Saturday amid reports Mauricio Pochettino is close to leaving for Manchester United. K League action resumes Nov. 21–22, and MLS's wild-card round is Nov. 19.
